html:
SMTO-EXE-0086 — The computer didn't let SMTO take a screenshot

GUID: a9d4813d-d023-5b99-af08-4938f74b56a2
Slug: screen-permission-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO asked the computer for a picture of its screen, but the system refused or sent back nothing. No screenshot was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On a Mac, open System Settings › Privacy & Security › Screen Recording and turn it on for the Gateway's program (or for Terminal, if you start the Gateway from Terminal). macOS blocks screenshots from any program that hasn't been given Screen Recording permission.
  2. When no task is using that Gateway, quit the Gateway on that computer and start it again. macOS only applies a new Screen Recording permission after the program restarts.
  3. On any computer, make sure it is unlocked, its desktop is showing and the screen is awake. The system won't hand over a picture of the screen while it is locked or the display is asleep.
  4. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a New chat and ask again. Checking refreshes what the Gateway can do, and a new chat uses that updated list.

What success looks like

  • SMTO takes the screenshot and attaches it to the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages that computer. Don't switch off the computer's security settings, and don't ask SMTO to capture a different computer's screen instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's native screen capture was refused or returned no image (macOS Screen Recording not granted or ScreenCaptureKit returned nothing, Windows BitBlt failed, X11 GetImage returned nothing, or a PermissionError was raised).

What this means

  • Screen-access checks or native capture calls refused access, returned no image, or raised PermissionError. This includes explicit macOS recording denial and lower-level capture failures without a narrower OS cause. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Screen-access checks or native capture calls refused access, returned no image, or raised PermissionError. This includes explicit macOS recording denial and lower-level capture failures without a narrower OS cause.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect platform readiness and permission detail; distinguish a missing permission from a native capture refusal before changing settings.

How to fix it

  • On macOS grant Screen Recording to the actual Gateway executable (or to Terminal if the Gateway is launched from it) in System Settings, restart the Gateway and refresh its capabilities. On Windows make sure the Gateway runs on the accessible interactive input desktop (unlocked); on Linux X11 confirm the session allows XGetImage. Check readiness unavailable_reason before the next explicit capture.
  • Check the indicated session or capture permission. Grant macOS Screen Recording only when required, settle active work before any restart, and verify readiness.

Retry and execution caution

  • On macOS grant Screen Recording to the Gateway executable in System Settings, then restart it and refresh Gateway metadata. On Windows use the accessible interactive input desktop.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended explicit capture succeeds under the selected session's deliberately granted permissions.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
